judgment.rationale: Both endpoints are Class-5 Content bullets (rank 4, identical coordinate) under the same Competency C-2.5 ('Identifies, describes and extends simple number patterns') and Curricular Goal CG-2. First is 'Patterns in division- Dividing by 10 and 100' with LCs 'Identify patterns in division when dividing numbers by 10/100'; second is 'Patterns in multiplication' with LCs identify/describe/extend patterns in multiplication. This is substantive same-topic coherence: pattern-seeking applied to two inverse arithmetic operations, mutually reinforcing within the same competency. However, both sit at the same developmental rank and the bounded evidence gives no pair-specific sequencing or increased-complexity signal (the division bullet is narrowed to dividing by 10/100 rather than a demonstrable extension of multiplication patterns), so no directional buildsTowards is asserted. Source evidence for both SFIs is truncated (24 omitted items each), which limits any finer sequencing judgment.

judgment.rationale: Both endpoints are Content bullets under Competency C-1.13 ('Develops computational thinking through problem solving strategies') within CG-1: Class-1 '• Assembling parts' (LC: assemble parts together as a problem solving strategy) and Class-2 '• Arranging pictures' (LC: arrange pictures in a logical order). They are coherent, complementary early computational-thinking activities involving organising components into a meaningful whole or sequence, so substantive conceptual coherence exists beyond the shared parent. However, the bounded text gives no evidence that assembling physical parts is a specific precursor whose proficiency supports logical picture sequencing; they are distinct strategies (construction vs. ordering) rather than a deepening or extension of one skill, so the permitted Class-1-to-Class-2 buildsTowards is not substantively supported. Source excerpts for both SFIs are truncated (24 omitted evidence items each), limiting further discrimination; the symmetric relatesTo is the defensible judgment.
